reciprocal.why: Both name action without forcing: wu wei in the Daoist texts, releasement in Heidegger's account of thinking.
Both are Heidegger's terms for a non-grasping relation to what is.
Both name an active release of the grip on outcomes; Eckhart's letting-go of self-will parallels the Buddhist release of craving.
Eckhart's negative virtues are Stoic-sounding: freedom won by releasing attachments rather than adding disciplines.
The waiting that expects nothing and the beginner's stance of not-knowing both keep the mind open to what arrives.
Both take what comes without the added struggle; Gelassenheit frames it as a release of willing.
Objectless sitting and objectless waiting are near neighbours: both hold awareness open without directing it at anything.
